capture.final_message:
Use the maximal-independent-set characterization of bases.

- For the first conjunct, choose a basis \(I\) of \(X\). Since \(I\) is independent and \(I\subseteq X\subseteq Y\), extend \(I\) to a basis \(J\) of \(Y\). This gives \(I\subseteq J\). It is precisely the standard basis-extension lemma represented by `Matroid.exists_isBasis_subset_isBasis`.

- For the second conjunct, show that the two matroids have the same bases. Given an \(M₁\)-base \(B₁\), it is \(M₂\)-independent by hypothesis, so extend it to an \(M₂\)-base \(B₂\) with \(B₁\subseteq B₂\). Then \(B₂\) is \(M₁\)-independent by the other hypothesis. Maximality of the \(M₁\)-base \(B₁\) forces \(B₁=B₂\), hence \(B₁\) is also an \(M₂\)-base. Repeat symmetrically, then apply matroid extensionality from equality of ground sets and equality of base families.

The common-ground-set assumption is essential: bases alone do not detect additional loop elements outside every base.
